Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and somewhat disorganized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Do not use regular dishwashing detergent. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free through the Coupang Experience Group event.

(몽키스패너는 필요합니다.)❇️ 대기중이나 사용중일때나 생각보다 훨씬 조용해요.뜨거운 온수로 세척을 하니 물 온도를 유지하기 위해대기중에도 약간의 소음이라도 있을줄 알았는데 그냥 조용해요.식기 세척중에도 업소용 세척기는 굉음이 나는데 반해미디어 식기세척기는 거슬리거나 스트레스를 받을 정도의 불편한 소음이 안나서 정말 좋았어요.❇️ 세척 시간이 65분이라길래 처음에는 놀랐어요.업소용 식기 세척기는 보통 1분 또는 1분30초인데무슨 차이가 왜 이렇게 많이 나는가 하고 알아보니업소용은 고압 모터나 물 온도를 더 높게 설정해두고수압과 스팀을 내보내는. 오로지 세척 하나만 생각하고 만들어져 있어서엄청난 소음이 생기고 전기도 많이 들어가는데에 비해가정용 식기 세척기는 크기나, 소비전력, 세척력, 소음을 고려하고살균기능이나 건조기능도 추가되니 그런만큼 시간이 늘어났나 보더라구요.미디어 식기 세척기는 세척 코스도 4가지나 되서요령것 시간 조절도 가능했어요.❇️ 자동 문열림 기능 최고에요.업소용 식기 세척기나 저희 누나집 식기 세척기는세척이 완료되면 자동으로 문열리는 기능이 없어서그 안에 열기와 습기가 그대로 머물러 있는데미디어 식기 세척기는 세척이 완료되면알림이 울리면서 문이 자동으로 탁 하고 열려있어요이거 정말 꿀 기능이에요.문이 자동으로 열리는 만큼 열기와 습기가 다 빠져서더 깔끔하게 뽀송뽀송 하게 건조되는것에 도움이 되요.보통 열기와 습기가 그대로 있는채로완료된지 모르고 놔둬버리면 하나도 건조가 안된상태로습해져 있을텐데 이 미디어 식기세척기는 돌려놓고깜빡하고 알림 소리를 못들어도 아무런 문제가 없어요.❇️ 다신 없이 못살정도의 편리함과 만족도.보통의 현대인들이 그렇겠지만 살아가려고 하루종일 애를 쓰고 살다보면집안일에 소홀해지기 마련이죠.저도 항상 집안일에 신경쓰려고 하지만퇴근하고 저녁을 먹고 난 후에 '설거지 바로 해야지...설거지 바로 해야지...' 라고 생각만 하고 그냥 담궈만 둔체하루 이틀 보내는 적이 많았어요. 너무 지치다 보니...근데 미디어 식기 세척기가 생기고 나서는 정말 삶이 깔끔하고 윤택해졌습니다.세상 이렇게 좋을 수가 없어요.설거지 거리가 많이 생기건 말건 컵도 그냥 한번 쓰고 새거 쓰고느긋하게 먹고 살살 행궈서 식기 세척기에 넣고 돌려두면알아서 다 해줍니다. 자동으로 문까지 열리는건 정말 최고중에 최고에요.고온에 살균에 위 아래 옆에서까지 물을 쏴주니 제가 손으로 꼼꼼하게 하는것보다도훨씬 깨끗합니다. 초초 대만족이에요.✴️✴️ 마무리 ✴️✴️이번에 미디어 식기 세척기를 사용해보면서정말 너무 너무 만족스러웠어요.아직 집에 식기 세척기가 없으시다면이 미디어 세척기를 구매해서 사용해 보시기를 강력 추천해요.주변에 저처럼 혼자 자취하는 친구들에게도 강력 추천했어요.부모님 집에도 하나 보내드려야 겠어요.진심으로 하는 말인데 한번도 안써본 사람은 있어도한번만 써본 사람은 없을 것 같아요.길고 정리가 부족한 글 읽어주셔서 감사합니다.* 미디어 식기 세척기를 구매하실때에쿠팡에서 판매하는 식기 세척기 전용 세제도 함께 구매하세요~일반 설거지 세제는 사용하시면 안됩니다~ 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Sentence (English): This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free through the Coupang Experience Group event.
Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and somewhat disorganized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Do not use regular dishwashing detergent. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free through the Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. You must not use regular dishwashing detergent. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free through the Coupang Experience Group event. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. You must not use regular dishwashing detergent. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free through the Coupang Experience Group event. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. You must not use regular dishwashing detergent. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free through the Coupang Experience Group event. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. You must not use regular dishwashing detergent. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free through the Coupang Experience Group event. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang.
