Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Sentence (English): In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time.
Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. You must not use regular dishwashing detergent. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free through the Coupang Experience Group event. Sentence (English): If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model.
Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. You must not use regular dishwashing detergent. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free through the Coupang Experience Group event. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Comments (English): [ There may be people who have never used it, but there are no people who have used it only once. ] || ---------------- || Having used commercial dishwashers for over 10 years, I had a great opportunity to try out a household dishwasher, so I used it for about two weeks. I will write a review, one by one, as honestly and straightforwardly as possible. - It doesn't take up much space. The commercial dishwashers I used before took up space vertically all the way to the ceiling and were very long horizontally, but the Midea dishwasher looks exactly like a microwave or oven, so it is small and cute (the width is said to be 55cm). Fortunately, it didn't take up as much space as I had feared, so I was able to make room for it in my small and cozy kitchen. Installation is very simple. (It seems easy to move.) Although a Rocket Installation technician schedules a visit in advance, I felt I should know how to do it myself just in case, so I asked various questions and watched the installation process carefully. Contrary to my worries, I was glad that I didn't necessarily have to drill holes in the sink or kitchen shelves. I was concerned after seeing the advertisement photos that I had to make holes, but it turned out that it is perfectly possible to install it without drilling any. (Of course, the appearance isn't quite as neat as it could be ^^). It is also much lighter than I expected. I think I can easily move it around if I ever want to change its location. I plan to install it myself after moving. (You will need a monkey wrench.) It is much quieter than I expected, whether in standby or in use. Since it washes with hot water, I expected some noise even while idle to maintain the water temperature, but it is just quiet. Unlike commercial dishwashers that make a deafening noise during washing, the Midea dishwasher didn't produce any annoying or stressful noise, which I really liked. I was surprised at first when I heard the wash time was 65 minutes. Commercial dishwashers usually run for 1 minute or 1 minute 30 seconds. I wondered why there was such a big difference, so I looked into it. I found that commercial models are designed solely for washing—using high-pressure motors and higher water temperatures to generate water pressure and steam—so they produce tremendous noise and consume a lot of electricity. In contrast, household dishwashers consider size, power consumption, cleaning performance, and noise levels... Since sterilization and drying functions have been added, it seems the time has increased accordingly. The Midea dishwasher has as many as four wash cycles, so I was able to adjust the time skillfully. The automatic door opening feature is the best. Commercial dishwashers and the one at my sister's house don't have this feature, so heat and humidity remain inside. But with the Midea dishwasher, when the wash is finished, an alert sounds and the door automatically snaps open. This is a truly amazing feature. Because the door opens automatically, all the heat and humidity escape, helping the clothes dry more thoroughly and fluffily. Usually, if you leave the dishwasher without realizing it's finished while the heat and humidity remain, the clothes will be damp and un-dried. But with this Midea dishwasher, even if you run it and forget to hear the alert, there is no problem at all. It offers such convenience and satisfaction that I can't live without it again. As is probably the case for most modern people, when you struggle all day just to make ends meet, it is inevitable that you neglect housework. I always try to pay attention to housework, too, but... After getting off work and having dinner, I used to often just think, "I should do the dishes right away. I should do them right away," but then leave them soaking for a day or two. I was just too exhausted. But ever since I got the Midea dishwasher, my life has truly become neat and comfortable. It couldn't be better. Whether there are a lot of dishes or not, I just use a cup once and then buy a new one. I eat leisurely, rinse gently, put it in the dishwasher, and run it. It takes care of everything automatically. The fact that the door opens automatically is truly the best of the best. With high temperature, sterilization, and water spraying from the top, bottom, and sides, it is much cleaner than if I washed them meticulously by hand. I am super, super satisfied. In conclusion, I was truly, truly satisfied using the Midea dishwasher this time. If you don't have a dishwasher at home yet, I highly recommend purchasing and trying this Midea model. I strongly recommended it to my friends who live alone like me. I think I should send one to my parents' house, too. I mean it sincerely: there may be people who have never used one, but I don't think there are any who have used one just once. Thank you for reading this long and poorly organized post. * When purchasing a Midea dishwasher, please also purchase the dishwasher-specific detergent sold on Coupang. Sentence (English): I purchased this dishwasher to replace a 19-year-old Bosch panel-front model, and unfortunately, the new technology is a downgrade.
Comments (English): [ Over-Engineered and Noisy ] || ---------------- || I purchased this dishwasher to replace a 19-year-old Bosch panel-front model, and unfortunately, the new technology is a downgrade. The much-touted "PowerControl" arm is more of a gimmick than a benefit—it's unnecessarily noisy, emitting an irritating plastic-like squeak during both washing and drying cycles. This noise is entirely audible and detracts from the overall experience. Additionally, it's far from the quiet operation Bosch was once known for. The complex, geared design feels like a failure point waiting to happen. To the designers constantly adding features: users don't need granular control over cleaning strength in specific quadrants of the bottom rack. We just want our dishes cleaned effectively and quietly. The PowerControl feature is impractical—nobody is using it. The noise issues don't stop there. During drying, the fan is significantly louder compared to older Bosch models, producing a persistent low hum throughout the excessively long drying cycle. This wasn't an issue with older designs, which were far quieter. The "CrystalDry" feature, another selling point, adds to the noise without delivering much value. On its own, CrystalDry leaves dishes wet; only by using the "Sanitize" option alongside it do you achieve an acceptable drying result. However, this comes at the cost of added heat, which may not be ideal for plastic items. The biggest disappointment is how far Bosch has strayed from its reputation for low-noise dishwashers. A standard cycle now takes a staggering three hours. While it's understandable that manufacturers must meet EPA water usage standards, Bosch could at least provide a truly effective, faster cycle. The "Speed 60" option is shorter but fails to include "Sanitize" or "CrystalDry," leaving dishes wet and impractical to use. Overall, Bosch seems to have lost touch with what consumers actually need: fast, efficient, and quiet dishwashers. Instead, these models are slow, over-engineered, and noisy. Bosch should revisit its priorities and focus on real-world functionality rather than unnecessary features.

Sentence (English): I want to give a dishwasher as a gift to my mother who recently moved to a new house.
Comments (English): I want to give a dishwasher as a gift to my mother who recently moved to a new house. Her health is not very good due to diabetes that suddenly came after my father passed away, but she is the head of the household and is old, but she still works as a caregiver. Since she works in three shifts, she does not have much time to be at home and does not have much time to do housework, so when she visits the house, there are piles of dishes and it breaks my heart. Since it can be controlled with the LG ThinQ app while she is working, she can just put the dishes in and leave when she is busy, and it is also convenient that it can be operated with a cell phone. The cutlery tray is located on the top shelf for easy use. It's good that it's separate and can be spread out, laid down one by one, inserted, and rotated, so it's good that frequently used dishes such as spoons and ladles are washed cleanly. I heard that a dishwasher with a large capacity is good, and although we are a family of two, there are a lot of dishes to wash when preparing meals, so a large capacity for 14 people would be perfect. I hope that my mother will have a lot of freedom in her daily life and mind by using a dishwasher. I think my mother will really like it because she will feel a convenience she's never felt before, her quality of life will improve, and the stress of washing dishes will be reduced. I want to give her one as a gift soon.
