Sentence (English): I had a Whirlpool dishwasher before I bought this one that I ABSOLUTELY loved.
Comments (English): [ Cheated on the bottom rack with that basket ] || ---------------- || I had a Whirlpool dishwasher before I bought this one that I ABSOLUTELY loved. It had the silverware basket IN THE DOOR. It made the bottom part of the dishwasher big enough to put bigger things in it and fit more odd sizes of dishes to wash. But it broke so I was looking for the same style and found out that Whirlpool quit making this style. WHAT A SHAME! I was so disappointed. But we needed a dishwasher, so we bought this one which had the basket on the bottom and the third level for smaller items and silverware. If you have a lot of silverware (especially for families), the top does not take it all and if you have items like odd pieces cookware, some may not fit on to. Then you are stuck having to use that basket on the bottom. I know you can take the basket out for big items, but that huge space when you take that silverware basket out does no good for loading additional plates, etc. along with the big items. What a waste of space there. Plus, when you take out the basket, you have to put it somewhere in your kitchen while the dishes are getting cleaned. I also noticed that when you use the quick wash, my dishes after it is cleaned are still wet, so I have to dry every single piece of items in the dishwasher. The normal wash takes 3 hours, and it does job if you have a full load that needs that good cleaning. My old one (using the quick one-hour wash) did not do that. The dishes came out dried. Another disappointment! Why, oh why, did Whirlpool changed that great silverware in the door design? Bring it back. It is too late for me. The control panel does show the actual time it takes to have the dishes cleaned. This dishwasher is very quiet. The price was good as it was on sale at Home Depot. The dishes do get cleaned up pretty good. However, my big complaint is that I feel cheated on the space on the bottom rack as you have to be more selective on what goes in with that big basket. I would give this a 3 1/2 STARS.

I could install myself, but I was happy for the no hassle experience. There were a couple of aspects of this KitchenAid dishwasher that I wasn't thrilled about, but it may be unique to my dishes, bowls, etc., and since I knew in advance, I was able to solve it so I still give it 5 stars. Nothing worse than bowls flopping forward! So knowing this in advance, and because the bottom rack of my dead dishwasher was the only thing I liked about it, I scabbed the bottom rack from it, and it fits perfectly in the KitchenAid. Problem solved. I also scabbed the wine glass stem holder and utensil caddy, both of which work nicely in my new dishwasher LOL

The one thing that is consistent is the high price for the KitchenAid products. They have lost a customer with the decline in quality. The next time my kitchen gets a makeover it will not be with KitchenAid appliances.

Comments (English): [ Worth the extra investment over cheaper models ] || ---------------- || The step up from our trusty-but-cheap dishwasher to this Bosch Series 6 has been night and day for our family of five.We took a leap of faith based on other people's feedback recommending series 6 for the build quality and it has been worth the investment.The layout is thoughtful and we seem to be able to fit everything in as needed without compromising on how clean the dishes come out. In the short time owning the dishwasher, we've also used the oven tray sprayer feature. Probably the most functional feature is the ability to shift the middle tray up-and-down trivially has meant we're doing decent full loads without playing too much dish tetris or holding back dishes to fit in another load.Unsurprisingly, this is yet another wifi-enabled whiteware, but what is surprising is the two features that we find really convenient: dishwasher finished notifications and the "smart start" that automatically delays the start to off-peak power time.Probably the only (minor) gripe is that the door is easy to close, but quite stiff to open, which is making it a little trickier for the young ones putting their dishes away. Also, there's a strip of plastic that comes with the dishwasher that looks to be for covering the bottom when the feet are extended, but it doesn't cover the whole height, nor stay in place.

Sentence (English): We waited for a sale on this dishwasher and still splurged on this dishwasher because we really loved the idea of all of our dishes actually being dry and not having to leave the door open while we waited for everything to dry.
Comments (English): [ Not as good as we were hoping for the price! ] || ---------------- || We waited for a sale on this dishwasher and still splurged on this dishwasher because we really loved the idea of all of our dishes actually being dry and not having to leave the door open while we waited for everything to dry. That, or we'd have to unload the plastics and put them in a drying rack. The mineral that it has inside does, in general, dry better than a dishwasher with just a normal heat element. However, if you have any containers or dishes with lips on them, then the water still just sits on them and doesn't dry. That means that we still need to leave the dishwasher open for containers to dry (after dumping the water) or have to put dishes in the drying rack. If you're only buying this dishwasher because that feature really appeals to you like it did us, then save your money and buy the Kitchen-aid that has a much better layout and bigger utensil basket than this one. One additional negative is that the tines are SO tilted that it minimizes the amount of dishes you can actually put in for each load. We have to run the dishwasher more often than we did with our old one (probably not an accident becaues the more we use the dishwasher, the quicker we'll need a new one). The layout isn't efficient. The one big plus I'll give it is that it's super quiet, like so quiet we're not usually sure if it's on and don't know when it's done. The 3rd rack that's adjustable with the feature to adjust just one side or both is also nice, but again, the Kitchen-Aid has more space, and we liked the layout better. Overall, it's a decent dishwasher, but the price is out of line with the features that don't work as well as you hope they will.

Sentence (English): I recently bought the LG DF587HVS dishwasher and I have to say that I am delighted with it.
Comments (English): [ EXCELLENT LG DISHWASHER ] || ---------------- || I recently bought the LG DF587HVS dishwasher and I have to say that I am delighted with it. I have to highlight its modern design and spectacular steel finish. Its electronic control panel is very intuitive to use and easy to handle. It has an energy rating of class A, with the consequent energy savings throughout the year. Another aspect that I liked is the reduced water consumption per wash cycle, 9.5 liters; as well as the reduced noise level that is practically inaudible during operation (it has 43 db) having a B rating. Inside it should be noted that it has two spray arms, one for each basket. Another detail to keep in mind is the possibility of adjusting the upper basket to accommodate larger than normal dishes, which is appreciated. The cutlery basket is worth mentioning, which leaves more space in the rest of the dishwasher and the possibility of also adjusting the height of part of it for when it is necessary to put in larger kitchen utensils such as saucepans, ladles or whatever is needed. In addition, there is the possibility of removing the cutlery basket if necessary. In short, an exceptional dishwasher that I recommend to anyone who wants to buy or change a dishwasher.

Tiene una clasificación energetica de clase A, con el  consiguiente ahorro energetico a lo largo del año. Otro aspecto que me ha gustado es el reducido consumo de agua por ciclo de lavado, 9.5 litros; así como el reducido nivel de ruido que en funcionamiento practicamente no se oys (tiene 43 db) teniendo una clasificación B. Comments (English): I have been using my new dishwasher for about a month now. This dishwasher cleanses well for the price point. I was disappointed with regard to loading dishes. The racks have very limited flexibility for adjusting to fit the kinds of dishes I have. Very frustrating. My rating is really like a 3.5 stars because of this annoying limitation. It is also a bit noisier than my previous LG that I paid way less money for, but it does wash and dry the dishes well, in less time. I guess they sacrificed the noise and basket flexibility to provide more digital options, which I don't use. I only use the Turbo extra dry option, which works very well. Comments (English): [ Cheap-feeling and poorly organized ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher in summer 2024, and unfortunately, I disliked it so much that I ended up replacing it three months later (at great expense because it was outside of the return window). I tried to live with it, but it was just too frustrating and disappointing.- The door feels cheap and flimsy, both the weight and the closing “seal” action. - The control buttons are on the outside, so they can be easily pressed accidentally by a toddler. - The control buttons aren't very responsive. You need to press and hold for long time, and when you do, there's no light to indicate something has been initiated. - Utensil race is very small and fills up quickly.- Lower rack prongs are too small for large pots and pans- Nothing dries- The adjustable plastic pieces on the inside could not be removed (ex: the wine glass fold outs). They took up space when not in use, and made it more difficult to maximize the space.We went back to a KitchenAid, which has a more secure door, better controls, and much better organization inside. The Bosch will probably work fine for you, but beware it feels like an extremely low-end dishwasher.

Sentence (English): I bought this high-end dishwasher from a high-end company, thinking it would be the last I'd have to worry about dishwashers for a long time.
Comments (English): [ Junk - watch out ] || ---------------- || I bought this high-end dishwasher from a high-end company, thinking it would be the last I'd have to worry about dishwashers for a long time. Not so. As far as I'm concerned, this machine is junk. 1. The top-mounted touch controls are hard to operate, especially with wet fingers. We consistently have to press several times with varying degrees of pressure to get the controls to work. 2. The "EasyGlide" rack system is a pain in the neck. Each time we want to move a rack up or down (e.g., for glasses), my wife and I together spend a number of minutes working on it. It's non-intuitive, easy to accidentally slip the rack off its track, and hard to get it back on. 3. The "CrystalDry" system is anything but. Our dishes are soaking wet every time . much worse than our old dishwasher. Bosch seems way behind the curve on this. 4. The "Home Connect" feature is non-intuitive and difficult to use. 5. Yesterday, this machine failed completely. The machine is only 1/2 year old. Now, the control panel doesn't work and we can't turn it on. 6. It's understandable that some percentage of new electronic gear will break -- hopefully, a small percentage. Not a problem, as long as customer service can take care of the issue. But when I called Bosch customer service, they informed me of only two companies in my major metro area that Bosch has authorized to do warranty repairs; and told me that the soonest someone could come and evaluate the issue is almost a week and a half from now, with the next appointment two weeks from now. That is abysmal customer service, after we spent >$2k (incl tax) on this machine just a half a year ago. There are many appliance repair techs that advertise "same day" service, which is what users hope for. I guess Bosch decided not to contract with them. So customers like me are out of luck. This is the opposite of a high-end experience.

I hope the new one lasts 10 years as well as the rust warranty. The 29-year-old washing machine is all stainless inside and has some rust only on one rack that was probably hit. Sentence (English): I really recommend this.
Comments (English): I really recommend this. I have a family of four, ages 3 and 6. The 12-person dishwasher we had before was an old version, so it didn't feel clean enough, and there were more dishes that didn't fit in the dishwasher than I thought. So, even though we didn't have a lot of dishes, I kept doing them by hand instead of using the dishwasher. But then I realized I was spending about 40 minutes a day doing the dishes. I washed them, put them away, and put the dishes away when they were dry. Sometimes the dishes didn't dry quickly, so I also had a dish dryer. So after much deliberation, I decided to buy a new dishwasher since we moved. Since we don't eat lunch at home, there isn't a lot of dishes to wash, so I was thinking of buying a 6-person one, and I did a lot of research. I watched Gwigom's YouTube videos and did a lot of research. I was thinking about buying a famous brand, but it was expensive for a 6-person one. Then I found out that it was made by this media. I didn't want to pay more than double the price. So I looked up reviews and decided to buy it since it was cheap. If it was good, I'd be happy. If not, I'd use it for a while and then replace it. I ordered it late in the evening, but it was installed the next day, which was so happy. I ran the dishwasher as soon as I got it. It's a bit hard to put in things like pots, but I was able to fit one. But it's easy to wash one pot, so I just put in dishes, cups, and spoons. If you don't stack them, it washes really clean. It really does look shinier than when I did it myself. Washing the kids' water bottles and straws was the hardest part, but I'm so happy. The straws and other parts wash better than I thought. Still, since they're for the kids, I feel a little uneasy, so after the dishwasher is done, I just rinse the straws and other parts in water. Things like water bottles, cups, and plates wash really well. I don't think there's any point in buying a dishwasher for pre-washing, so I just collect the dishes in the dishwashing bin I already have. Then, there is no need to pre-wash separately. However, if something like cheese gets on it, it really doesn't wash off well even if you wash it by hand. You have to check it once in a while. But I am very satisfied and using it well! I really recommend it. And since it is a two-tier, it is small on the side. What is this? On the sink top. Anyway, I really like that it doesn't take up much space. And for your information, Frog detergent is the best. I bought Nelly's because I have kids, but it gets on water stains.

Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): [ Things to know before use and honest reviews! ] || ---------------- || Pros: Powerful cleaning, automatic door opening, ample storage space. User review: Hello. Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): [ Things to know before use and honest reviews! ] || ---------------- || Pros: Powerful cleaning, automatic door opening, ample storage space. User review: Hello. Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Today, I'm going to review the "Media Auto-Open Dishwasher for 6 People." If you're in a hurry, just read the overall review at the bottom. Media Auto-Open Dishwasher, Satisfactory Features: After using the Media dishwasher, I've found it to be a truly effective dishwasher. First, powerful cleaning: I've always questioned the cleaning power of dishwashers when washing dishes by hand. No matter how much people rave about their effectiveness, I've always wondered if they could clean dishes as thoroughly as if I'd washed them by hand. Contrary to my concerns, they actually clean dishes much more thoroughly than by hand. To test the effectiveness, I put in dishes with red stains from yukgaejang (Korean beef soup) and tteokbokki (stir-fried rice cakes). They came out clean, with no trace of food left. (See photos.) Second, ample storage space: It's hard to gauge the size from the detailed description or review photos. It's described as a slim size and is meant for six people, so I thought it would be compact, but it's much larger than I expected. It has a two-tier basket and can hold everything from small dishes like seasoning bowls to large plates, cups, and spoons. I was initially surprised by how large it was, but I realized it's even better for storing a lot of dishes at once. Even for a six-person dishwasher this big, I don't think I'll ever run out of room for more. Third, the auto-open door function: The dishwasher runs for 65 minutes by default. When there are about five minutes left after the cycle is complete, the door automatically opens. This quickly expels moist air and allows outside air to naturally dry the dishes, effectively removing odors and moisture. I think the auto-open door function is essential for a dishwasher. Overall, the three-stage wash system—high, medium, and low—cleans thoroughly, leaving no trace of food stains. It even removes red liquid completely. It cleans dishes better than washing them by hand. (See photo) There's ample storage space, and the noise level isn't as loud as I thought, so it wasn't a bother. I also liked the minimal or no-punching capability. Personally, I tend to avoid using complicated machines, but I also liked the simplicity of the operation. I loved everything about the design, performance, and how to use it, so I couldn't find a single thing I was disappointed with. I'm truly satisfied. Finally, for those who are new to dishwashers, I'll wrap up by listing a few things to keep in mind before use! 1. Be sure to use dishwasher-specific detergent. Using regular detergent can cause the dishwasher to malfunction. For liquid detergent, place it where shown in the photo, and for solid detergent, place one tablet on the bottom of the dishwasher. 2. For dishes with grease, red pepper powder, or red juice, be sure to rinse them with water before putting them back in. 3. Make sure the auto door open function is enabled and turn it on. Sometimes, if it's not enabled, the door won't open automatically after washing. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Sentence (English): I highly recommend this.
Comments (English): I highly recommend this. We are a family of four with children aged 3 and 6. Our old 12-place setting dishwasher was an older model, so it didn't feel like it cleaned things very thoroughly. Also, I realized that there are more children's dishes than I thought shouldn't be put in the dishwasher. So, even though we didn't have much to do, I just kept washing them by hand rather than using the dishwasher. But at some point, I realized I was spending about 40 minutes a day on washing dishes. Washing, tidying up, and putting away dishes once they dried—and since the dishes didn't always dry quickly, we also had a dish dryer on hand. So, after much deliberation, I decided to buy a new dishwasher since we had just moved. Since none of us eat lunch at home, there isn't a huge amount of dishwashing, so I looked into buying a 6-place setting model and did a lot of research. I learned a lot by watching Gwigom's YouTube videos. I was planning to buy one from a famous brand, but it was expensive for a 6-place setting. However, when I found out that this brand was manufactured and imported by [Company Name], I didn't want to pay more than double the price. So, after looking up reviews, I decided to buy it just because it was cheap. I figured if it was good, great, and if not, I could use it for a while and replace it. I was so happy that even though I ordered late in the evening, it was installed the very next day. I ran the dishwasher as soon as I received it. It is a bit difficult to put things like pots in, but one does fit. Still, since washing a pot is easy, I mainly put in dishes, cups, and cutlery. If you put them in without stacking them, they wash really well and thoroughly. They actually look shinier than when I used to wash them myself. Washing the kids' water bottles and straws used to be the hardest part, so I am so happy now. The straws and parts wash better than I expected. Still, since it's for the kids, I feel a bit uneasy about it, so after the dishwasher finishes, I rinse just the straws and parts in water. It really cleans water bottles, cups, and dishes very well. I believe that pre-washing defeats the purpose of buying a dishwasher, so I collect the dishes in a basin filled with water that I normally use. So, you don't need to pre-wash separately; you can just put them directly into the dishwasher, and since there's no need to soak, they wash up really well. However, if the kids get things like cheese on them... that really doesn't come off easily even with hand washing, so you definitely have to check it from time to time. Still, I'm very satisfied and using it well! I highly recommend it, seriously. Also, since it's a two-tier unit, it takes up less space sideways—what is this? On the sink countertop... Anyway, I love that it doesn't take up much space. And for reference, I found the Frog brand detergent to be the best. Since I have kids, I tried buying Nellie's, but that one leaves water stains.

Comments (English): I highly recommend this. We are a family of four with children aged 3 and 6. Our old 12-place setting dishwasher was an older model, so it didn't feel like it cleaned things very thoroughly. Also, I realized that there are more children's dishes than I thought shouldn't be put in the dishwasher. Washing, tidying up, and putting away dishes once they dried—and since the dishes didn't always dry quickly, we also had a dish dryer on hand. So, after much deliberation, I decided to buy a new dishwasher since we had just moved. Since none of us eat lunch at home, there isn't a huge amount of dishwashing, so I looked into buying a 6-place setting model and did a lot of research. I learned a lot by watching Gwigom's YouTube videos. I was planning to buy one from a famous brand, but it was expensive for a 6-place setting. However, when I found out that this brand was manufactured and imported by [Company Name], I didn't want to pay more than double the price. So, after looking up reviews, I decided to buy it just because it was cheap. I figured if it was good, great, and if not, I could use it for a while and replace it. I was so happy that even though I ordered late in the evening, it was installed the very next day. I ran the dishwasher as soon as I received it. It is a bit difficult to put things like pots in, but one does fit. Still, since washing a pot is easy, I mainly put in dishes, cups, and cutlery. If you put them in without stacking them, they wash really well and thoroughly. They actually look shinier than when I used to wash them myself. Washing the kids' water bottles and straws used to be the hardest part, so I am so happy now. The straws and parts wash better than I expected. Still, since it's for the kids, I feel a bit uneasy about it, so after the dishwasher finishes, I rinse just the straws and parts in water. It really cleans water bottles, cups, and dishes very well. Sentence (English): So, even though we didn't have much to do, I just kept washing them by hand rather than using the dishwasher.
Comments (English): I highly recommend this. We are a family of four with children aged 3 and 6. Our old 12-place setting dishwasher was an older model, so it didn't feel like it cleaned things very thoroughly. Also, I realized that there are more children's dishes than I thought shouldn't be put in the dishwasher. So, even though we didn't have much to do, I just kept washing them by hand rather than using the dishwasher. But at some point, I realized I was spending about 40 minutes a day on washing dishes. Washing, tidying up, and putting away dishes once they dried—and since the dishes didn't always dry quickly, we also had a dish dryer on hand. So, after much deliberation, I decided to buy a new dishwasher since we had just moved. Since none of us eat lunch at home, there isn't a huge amount of dishwashing, so I looked into buying a 6-place setting model and did a lot of research. I learned a lot by watching Gwigom's YouTube videos. I was planning to buy one from a famous brand, but it was expensive for a 6-place setting. However, when I found out that this brand was manufactured and imported by [Company Name], I didn't want to pay more than double the price. So, after looking up reviews, I decided to buy it just because it was cheap. I figured if it was good, great, and if not, I could use it for a while and replace it. I was so happy that even though I ordered late in the evening, it was installed the very next day. I ran the dishwasher as soon as I received it. It is a bit difficult to put things like pots in, but one does fit. Still, since washing a pot is easy, I mainly put in dishes, cups, and cutlery. If you put them in without stacking them, they wash really well and thoroughly. They actually look shinier than when I used to wash them myself. Washing the kids' water bottles and straws used to be the hardest part, so I am so happy now. The straws and parts wash better than I expected. Still, since it's for the kids, I feel a bit uneasy about it, so after the dishwasher finishes, I rinse just the straws and parts in water. It really cleans water bottles, cups, and dishes very well. I believe that pre-washing defeats the purpose of buying a dishwasher, so I collect the dishes in a basin filled with water that I normally use. So, you don't need to pre-wash separately; you can just put them directly into the dishwasher, and since there's no need to soak, they wash up really well. However, if the kids get things like cheese on them... that really doesn't come off easily even with hand washing, so you definitely have to check it from time to time. Still, I'm very satisfied and using it well! I highly recommend it, seriously. Also, since it's a two-tier unit, it takes up less space sideways—what is this? On the sink countertop...
